It's crazy how my entire Linkedin feed is about Claude but no one actually properly explains it. I made this quick note for my team on how to start:

1. Models change all of the time. Today, use this:

☑ Fable-5-High on the first 1/2 prompts.
☑ Then switch to Opus-5-High (or Low).
☑ If it's a quick search, Grok or ChatGPT.

Yes, we pay for everything. And we have the $100/mo tier from Claude (and we never hit limits).

If you can't pay for anything, ChatGPT's model is pretty good (August 2026). Claude never tried to serve the free tiers people, so don't bother.

2. I stopped with .md files months ago. Instead:

☑ Skills for anything task you do more than twice.
☑ One Project per thing you work on weekly.
☑ Files only if it's a one-off doc I'll not open again.

Every skill I (personally) use is free to download. Just subscribe at https://t.co/psB7XxAv8w & I'll email you the link. 

3. Ignore the advice of 'write instructions':

☑ No custom instructions.
☑ No "you are an expert in…" paragraph.
☑ No context I paste into chats.

Every instruction you add is a rule Claude follows instead of thinking (outside of the box). You're paying for the smartest thing on the planet & then telling it to stay in a box.

4. Claude is not an image model (yet). So:

☑ Use ChatGPT for images (August 2026).
☑ If you still want Claude, ask for the image as HTML code.

The HTML thing sounds weird, but text in a generated image comes out incorrect. In HTML it's just text, so it's always right.

5. Your chat gets worse the longer it is. Instead:

☑ New task, new chat.
☑ It forgot something from 20 prompts ago? New chat.

Anthropic's own engineers said this. People keep one chat open for 3 weeks & then complain that Claude doesn't get them. 

6. Stop obsessing over prompts. Instead:

☑ "Ask me 10 questions before you start."
☑ Answer them badly, in the "Something else" option with your context.
☑ Then let it run.

The stuff in your head that you didn't type is the main problem. This is the highest ROI line in this whole note & it takes 4 mins.

7. Research mode is already in your app. The beast:

☑ Use it for anything you'd Google for 40 mins.
☑ Don't use it for quick stuff, it's slow.

Huge difference between "here's a summary" & "here's 40 sources I actually went & read." I don't know why this is hidden.

8. When it gives you a link, click it:

☑ AI writes the answer first, then goes looking for a page that agrees with it.
☑ 60% of high-credibility sites now block AI crawlers.
☑ 1 in 6 sources cited by AI search was written by another AI.

So it's reading AI slop. This is bonkers & almost nobody knows it. 

9. Don't be stupid with access:

☑ Never paste logins, passwords, or keys.
☑ Not explaining this one.

Everyone connects 14 tools on day one & then panics about permissions.

If you do one thing from this, do # 2. Download my skills at https://t.co/psB7XxAv8w. Upload them in Claude. Stop unnecessarily wasting 6 months figuring out which ones matter.

Ever wonder why training AI to create images and videos eats up so much computing power?

Researchers at the University of Science and Technology of China and https://t.co/411myyJ4gs present DMSampler!

DMSampler replaces slow 50-step sampling with a fast 4-to-8-step distilled model that acts as a quick proxy for the AI policy. It keeps updating itself alongside the policy so the samples stay accurate and aligned throughout training.

It outperforms previous diffusion RL methods on OCR, GenEval, and VBench benchmarks while cutting GPU hours by an order of magnitude.

Distillation Models are Good Samplers for Diffusion Reinforcement Learning
